summary: External regulatory updates are monitored and logged manually by Regulatory Affairs, screened for applicability, then assessed for impact by QA with e-mail-based input from subject matter experts. Changes are risk-classified, entered as a Change Request in the eQMS, reviewed by Compliance, approved at a weekly Change Control Board, and implemented through controlled document revisions and LMS training before QA verifies and closes the change. The median end-to-end cycle is 48 business days against a 30-day target.

roles.name: Regulatory Affairs Specialist
responsibilities: Log updates in the Regulatory Intelligence Log

roles.name: QA Analyst
responsibilities: Verify implementation and close the Change Request

roles.name: Subject Matter Experts
responsibilities: Provide functional impact input within 5 business days

roles.name: Process Owner
responsibilities: Create the Change Request in the eQMS

roles.name: Head of Quality and Site Head
responsibilities: Approve High risk changes with Part 11 electronic signatures

roles.name: Document Control Specialist
responsibilities: Revise and issue controlled documents in the DMS
Set effective dates and archive superseded versions

roles.name: Training Coordinator
responsibilities: Assign and track training in the LMS

systems.name: Regulatory Intelligence Log (Excel)
systems.purpose: Controlled spreadsheet recording incoming regulatory updates and applicability decisions

systems.name: RA shared drive
systems.purpose: Archive of downloaded source regulatory documents

systems.name: E-mail
systems.purpose: SME impact requests, follow-ups, reminders and CCB coordination

systems.name: eQMS
systems.purpose: Change Request records, approvals, electronic signatures and closure

systems.name: DMS
systems.purpose: Controlled document revision, approval and issuance

systems.name: SOP master list (Excel)
systems.purpose: Inventory of controlled procedures used to identify affected documents

steps.name: Receipt and Logging of Regulatory Update
steps.description: The RA Specialist reviews FDA, EMA, ICH and pharmacopoeial sources plus an e-mail digest each business day, logs each potentially relevant item in the Regulatory Intelligence Log with metadata, and archives the source document on the shared drive.
steps.input: Regulatory source publications; regulatory intelligence e-mail digest
steps.output: RIL entry with source, date, title, URL, type and authority; archived source document
pain_points: Approximately 40 items per week must be manually monitored and logged
Only ~8% of items are ultimately applicable, so most effort is spent on irrelevant updates
Only 71% of applicable updates are identified within 2 business days

steps.name: Initial Review and Applicability Determination
steps.description: The RA Specialist reads the full source document, determines whether it applies to any Meridian product, process, site, registration or system, records the rationale in the RIL, and prepares a two-page Regulatory Summary for applicable items. Not Applicable decisions are countersigned by the RA Manager.
steps.input: Source regulatory document; RIL entry; product and site registration list
steps.output: Applicability rationale; Regulatory Summary (FRM-RA-042-02); RA Manager countersign
steps.decision_description: Applicable or Not Applicable to Meridian operations
pain_points: 2 to 4 hours of full-document reading per item, repeated across ~40 items per week
Manager countersign adds up to 5 business days of waiting

steps.name: Impact Assessment
steps.description: The QA Analyst identifies candidate affected areas from the SOP master list, product register and validated systems inventory, e-mails SMEs for functional input, chases responses, resolves conflicts through follow-up meetings and consolidates a final Impact Assessment form.
steps.input: Regulatory Summary; SOP master list; product register; validated systems inventory
steps.output: Completed Impact Assessment form (FRM-QA-042-01) listing affected documents, processes, products and systems
pain_points: 7 to 12 business days elapsed, mostly waiting for SME responses
Average 3.2 follow-up e-mails per SME per assessment
Affected documents identified by manual search of spreadsheets rather than content matching

steps.name: Risk Classification
steps.description: The QA Manager reviews the completed Impact Assessment, assigns a Low, Medium or High risk classification using ICH Q9 principles, documents the rationale and determines the approval pathway.
steps.output: Risk Classification with rationale; approval pathway
steps.decision_description: Low / Medium / High risk and corresponding approval pathway
pain_points: 2 to 3 business days waiting for QA Manager availability for a 1 to 2 hour task
Classification criteria are rule-like but applied manually

steps.name: Change Request Creation
steps.description: The Process Owner creates a Change Request in the eQMS, completing 14 mandatory fields, attaching the Regulatory Summary, Impact Assessment and source document, and defining implementation action items with owners and due dates.
steps.input: Regulatory Summary; Impact Assessment form; Risk Classification
steps.output: Change Request record in eQMS with attachments and action plan
pain_points: About 60% of the 1.5 to 2.5 hours is re-entering information already captured in the IA form and Regulatory Summary

steps.name: Compliance and Regulatory Review
steps.description: The Compliance Officer confirms the regulatory interpretation, policy alignment, data integrity coverage and completeness of actions; the RA Manager determines whether a regulatory submission is required and documents the filing strategy. Comments are returned through the eQMS until closed.
steps.output: Compliance review record; filing strategy; closed review comments
steps.decision_description: Review complete or return with comments; regulatory submission required or not
pain_points: Average 1.6 review cycles per Change Request
3 to 5 business days elapsed

steps.name: Change Control Board Approval
steps.description: Medium and High risk Change Requests are presented at the weekly Tuesday CCB by the Process Owner. The board approves, rejects or returns the CR; High risk changes additionally require Part 11 electronic signatures from the Head of Quality and Site Head. Low risk CRs are approved electronically without CCB.
steps.output: Approval decision with electronic signatures; CCB minutes recorded in eQMS
pain_points: Average 4.5 business days waiting for the weekly meeting
20% of CRs are returned for more information and re-presented the following week

steps.name: Documentation Update
steps.description: The Document Control Specialist initiates revisions in the DMS for each affected document; authors prepare redlines; Document Control verifies formatting, numbering and cross-references; documents are routed for approval and given an effective date typically 30 days after approval.
steps.input: Approved Change Request; current controlled documents
steps.output: Approved revised documents with effective dates; superseded versions archived
pain_points: 10 to 15 business days per document set
3 to 4 hours of Document Control effort per document, average 4 documents per change
1.4 documentation errors per document set found at QA review

steps.name: Training Assignment and Completion
steps.description: The Training Coordinator identifies affected personnel via the LMS curriculum matrix, assigns read-and-understand or instructor-led training depending on risk, monitors completion weekly, sends reminders and escalates when completion is below 95% five days before the effective date.
steps.output: Training assignments; completion records; escalation notices
pain_points: 20 to 30 calendar days elapsed
4 to 6 hours of coordinator effort largely spent on manual reminders and reporting

steps.name: Implementation Verification and Change Closure
steps.description: The QA Analyst verifies all action items are complete, documents are effective, training completion is at least 95% and any submissions are filed; schedules a 90-day effectiveness check for High risk changes; closes the CR in the eQMS and updates the RIL.
steps.input: Change Request record; DMS status; LMS completion report; submissions tracker
steps.output: Closed Change Request; effectiveness check schedule; updated RIL
steps.decision_description: Verification passed and CR closed, or actions outstanding
pain_points: Verification requires manually cross-checking four separate systems

key_pain_points: High-volume manual monitoring: ~40 regulatory items per week are read and logged by hand although only ~8% are applicable
Impact assessment depends on e-mail coordination with SMEs, taking 7 to 12 business days with 3.2 follow-ups per SME
Information is re-keyed across the RIL, IA form and eQMS; ~60% of Change Request creation effort is duplicate data entry
Approval waits dominate elapsed time: 2 to 3 days for risk classification, 3 to 5 days for compliance review, 4.5 days for the weekly CCB
20% of Change Requests are returned by the CCB and 1.6 compliance review cycles are typical, indicating quality issues in upstream preparation
Documentation and training phases run 10 to 15 and 20 to 30 days respectively, with 1.4 errors per document set
Median end-to-end cycle of 48 business days versus a 30-day target
regulatory_references: 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures
EudraLex Volume 4 Chapter 1 and Annex 15 Section 11
